content.title: About
content.content: A muffin with raisins is a soft baked good made from wheat flour, eggs, milk, butter, and sugar, with raisins added for sweetness and texture. It has a light vanilla aroma, a subtle raisin flavor, and a tender, slightly moist crumb.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Muffins originated in England in the 19th century as a quick way to use leftover batter.
Raisins not only add sweetness but also retain moisture, keeping the muffin juicy.
Traditionally muffins are baked in paper liners, which make serving and transport easy.
In the United States blueberry muffins are popular, but raisins remain a classic European variant.
Gluten‑free muffin versions exist, using rice or almond flour instead of wheat.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrates provide quick energy, making the muffin a convenient snack.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Raisins are rich in dietary fiber, which supports healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The batter and raisins supply thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Raisins contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Muffins provide iron, potassium, and magnesium, contributing to overall nutrition.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Raisins and added sugar make the muffin calorie‑dense and can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, which is unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Butter adds saturated fats; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Muffins with raisins can be enjoyed as a stand‑alone snack, split and spread with cream cheese, added to yogurt, or served to children. Warm muffins are especially aromatic.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store muffins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in the oven or microwave before eating.
